questions.q: What is the single most important diagnostic step when checking a visual's number?
options: Rebuilding the entire page from scratch
Re-running the T-SQL extract
Clicking the visual and checking the exact measure name in the Fields pane's Values well, not trusting the title text
Reading the card's title text
questions.explain: A visual's title has no relationship to which measure actually feeds it -- the Values well binding decides the number.

questions.q: What does the controlled test in this lesson involve?
options: Adding a second card bound explicitly to [Total Sales], filtering to the same territory, and comparing it to the suspect card
Deleting the suspect card immediately
Changing the DimTerritory table's relationship type
Rewriting the CALCULATE formula inside [Total Sales (All Territories)]
questions.explain: Changing exactly one variable (which measure a new card uses) and observing the result confirms the hypothesis.

questions.q: What does ALL(DimTerritory) inside Total Sales (All Territories) remove?
options: Any filter currently applied through the DimTerritory relationship, including the page's own territory slicer
The DimTerritory table from the model entirely
Nothing -- ALL only affects visuals, not filters
Only filters applied to DimCustomer
questions.explain: ALL(DimTerritory) strips the territory filter specifically, which is exactly why the mis-bound card ignores the slicer.

questions.q: Why did the mis-binding go unnoticed when the page was first built in Lesson 11?
options: With no territory filter applied yet, both measures returned the same number by coincidence
Power BI displayed a warning that was ignored
DimTerritory didn't exist yet at that point
The headline card was hidden from view
questions.explain: ALL has nothing to strip away when nothing is filtered, so both measures matched until a slicer actually narrowed something down.

questions.q: Why is this bug described as a binding mistake rather than a formula mistake?
options: DimTerritory's relationship to Fact is broken
ALL(DimTerritory) is the wrong function to use anywhere in this model
The CALCULATE formula itself contains a syntax error
Total Sales (All Territories) is correctly written and still needed elsewhere; the issue is which measure a specific visual happens to use
questions.explain: The measure's DAX is legitimate and used correctly elsewhere (as the Pct of Company Total denominator) -- only the card's binding is wrong.
